# gba-emu: rules for every agent

Read PLAN.md before starting. It defines the phases, the shared contracts and who owns which file.
The benchmark lives at `/var/www/html/test-projects/gba-eval`, referred to below as `$GBA_EVAL`.
Use that absolute path; relative paths break inside worktrees.

## Originality (hard rule)
- Write all code yourself. Do not read, copy, or paraphrase any existing emulator:
  `$GBA_EVAL/candidates/` (gba-core), `$GBA_EVAL/third_party/` (Mesen2),
  `$GBA_EVAL/reference/mesen_step.cpp`, or mGBA/NanoBoyAdvance/VBA/etc. from memory or the web.
- Allowed sources: `$GBA_EVAL/spec/gbatek.htm` (GBA, ARM and THUMB chapters only), `$GBA_EVAL/spec/ABI.md`,
  `$GBA_EVAL/spec/gba_bios_stub.h`, the grader's outputs (scores, `.ref.png` vs `.cand.png`),
  and running ROMs from `$GBA_EVAL/corpus/roms/`.
- No per-ROM hacks: never branch on a ROM's hash, title, or game code. Fix the hardware behavior.

## Code readability
- Use clear, descriptive names for functions, variables and types: `destination_register`, `shift_amount`,
  `fn execute_data_processing`. Never cryptic ones like `x`, `t`, `rd2` or `tmp`. Loop indices
  (`i`, `line`) are fine when the meaning is obvious.
- Official gbatek register and field names are allowed (`DISPCNT`, `BG0CNT`, `IE`, `IF`, `CPSR`, `Rd`, `Rn`),
  each with a short plain-English comment where it is defined, e.g. `const DISPCNT: u32 = 0x000; // display control`.
- Every non-obvious function gets a one-line doc comment naming the gbatek section it implements, e.g.
  `/// Barrel shifter for data-processing operand 2 (gbatek: ARM Opcodes: Data Processing (ALU)).`
- Prefer small readable functions over clever one-liners. Split a long `match` arm or a dense bit-twiddling
  expression into a named helper.

## Ownership
- Only edit the files your task owns (see the ownership tables in PLAN.md).
- Shared files (`src/lib.rs`, `src/gba.rs`, `src/bus.rs`, `src/io.rs`, `src/irq.rs`, `src/scheduler.rs`,
  `Cargo.toml`) are changed only by the integrator (the executor session). If you need a contract
  change, say so in your report instead of making it.

## Git
- Remote: https://github.com/Rohan-Jalil/gba-eval-trial-rohan. Never push; the human pushes.
- Author and committer: Rohan Jalil <[REDACTED:email]>. This is set in this repo's git config;
  do not override it.
- Use Conventional Commits: `type(scope): summary`, for example `feat(cpu): add ARM data-processing ops`,
  `fix(ppu): wrap affine BG coordinates`, `test(timer): cascade overflow`, `docs(notes): phase 1 decisions`,
  `chore(results): phase 1 milestone`. Scopes: cpu, arm, thumb, bus, io, irq, ppu, apu, dma, timer,
  keypad, cart, abi, scripts, plan, notes, results.
- Commit after every meaningful step (a working instruction group, a passing test, a merged branch),
  not one large commit per phase.
- Worker agents commit on their own branch. Only the integrator merges into `main` (`git merge --no-ff`).

## Logging
- `NOTES.md`: add an entry for every decision or change of approach (date, what, why), and for every
  phase record which agents ran and on which model. The integrator writes the agent/model rows.
- `TIMELOG.md` belongs to the human. Agents never edit it.
- Milestones: `scripts/grade-full.sh <phase> "<note>"` saves `results/milestones/<phase>/`. Commit that
  folder and `scores.tsv`. All other `results/` output stays ignored.

## Before you report done
1. `cargo test` passes.
2. `cargo build --release --lib --target wasm32-unknown-unknown` succeeds.
3. `scripts/grade-subset.sh target/wasm32-unknown-unknown/release/gba_emu.wasm <name> <your tests> <smoke set>`.
   Report the per-test scores, and never lower a smoke-set score without saying so.
4. Your work is committed on your branch, and your report lists the commits.

LCD I/O BG Rotation/Scaling

4000028h - BG2X_L - BG2 Reference Point X-Coordinate, lower 16 bit (W)
400002Ah - BG2X_H - BG2 Reference Point X-Coordinate, upper 12 bit (W)
400002Ch - BG2Y_L - BG2 Reference Point Y-Coordinate, lower 16 bit (W)
400002Eh - BG2Y_H - BG2 Reference Point Y-Coordinate, upper 12 bit (W)
These registers are replacing the BG scrolling registers which are used for
Text mode, ie. the X/Y coordinates specify the source position from inside of
the BG Map/Bitmap of the pixel to be displayed at upper left of the GBA
display. The normal BG scrolling registers are ignored in Rotation/Scaling and
Bitmap modes.

  Bit   Expl.
  0-7   Fractional portion (8 bits)
  8-26  Integer portion    (19 bits)
  27    Sign               (1 bit)
  28-31 Not used

Because values are shifted left by eight, fractional portions may be specified
in steps of 1/256 pixels (this would be relevant only if the screen is actually
rotated or scaled). Normal signed 32bit values may be written to above
registers (the most significant bits will be ignored and the value will be
cut-down to 28bits, but this is no actual problem because signed values have
set all MSBs to the same value).

Internal Reference Point Registers
The above reference points are automatically copied to internal registers
during each vblank, specifying the origin for the first scanline. The internal
registers are then incremented by dmx and dmy after each scanline.
Caution: Writing to a reference point register by software outside of the
Vblank period does immediately copy the new value to the corresponding internal
register, that means: in the current frame, the new value specifies the origin
of the <current> scanline (instead of the topmost scanline).

4000020h - BG2PA - BG2 Rotation/Scaling Parameter A (alias dx) (W)
4000022h - BG2PB - BG2 Rotation/Scaling Parameter B (alias dmx) (W)
4000024h - BG2PC - BG2 Rotation/Scaling Parameter C (alias dy)  (W)
4000026h - BG2PD - BG2 Rotation/Scaling Parameter D (alias dmy) (W)

  Bit   Expl.
  0-7   Fractional portion (8 bits)
  8-14  Integer portion    (7 bits)
  15    Sign               (1 bit)

See below for details.

400003Xh - BG3X_L/H, BG3Y_L/H, BG3PA-D - BG3 Rotation/Scaling Parameters
Same as above BG2 Reference Point, and Rotation/Scaling Parameters, for BG3
respectively.

dx (PA) and dy (PC)
When transforming a horizontal line, dx and dy specify the resulting gradient
and magnification for that line. For example:
Horizontal line, length=100, dx=1, and dy=1. The resulting line would be drawn
at 45 degrees, f(y)=1/1*x. Note that this would involve that line is magnified,
the new length is SQR(100^2+100^2)=141.42. Yup, exactly - that's the old a^2 +
b^2 = c^2 formula.

dmx (PB) and dmy (PD)
These values define the resulting gradient and magnification for transformation
of vertical lines. However, when rotating a square area (which is surrounded by
horizontal and vertical lines), then the desired result should be usually a
rotated <square> area (ie. not a parallelogram, for example).
Thus, dmx and dmy must be defined in direct relationship to dx and dy, taking
the example above, we'd have to set dmx=-1, and dmy=1, f(x)=-1/1*y.

Area Overflow
In result of rotation/scaling it may often happen that areas outside of the
actual BG area become moved into the LCD viewport. Depending of the Area
Overflow bit (BG2CNT and BG3CNT, Bit 13) these areas may be either displayed
(by wrapping the BG area), or may be displayed transparent.
This works only in BG modes 1 and 2. The area overflow is ignored in Bitmap
modes (BG modes 3-5), the outside of the Bitmaps is always transparent.

--- more details and confusing or helpful formulas ---

The following parameters are required for Rotation/Scaling

  Rotation Center X and Y Coordinates (x0,y0)
  Rotation Angle                      (alpha)
  Magnification X and Y Values        (xMag,yMag)

The display is rotated by 'alpha' degrees around the center.
The displayed picture is magnified by 'xMag' along x-Axis (Y=y0) and 'yMag'
along y-Axis (X=x0).

Calculating Rotation/Scaling Parameters A-D

  A = Cos (alpha) / xMag    ;distance moved in direction x, same line
  B = Sin (alpha) / xMag    ;distance moved in direction x, next line
  C = Sin (alpha) / yMag    ;distance moved in direction y, same line
  D = Cos (alpha) / yMag    ;distance moved in direction y, next line


Calculating the position of a rotated/scaled dot
Using the following expressions,

  x0,y0    Rotation Center
  x1,y1    Old Position of a pixel (before rotation/scaling)
  x2,y2    New position of above pixel (after rotation scaling)
  A,B,C,D  BG2PA-BG2PD Parameters (as calculated above)

the following formula can be used to calculate x2,y2:

  x2 = A(x1-x0) + B(y1-y0) + x0
  y2 = C(x1-x0) + D(y1-y0) + y0






  
  LCD I/O Window Feature

The Window Feature may be used to split the screen into four regions. The
BG0-3,OBJ layers and Color Special Effects can be separately enabled or
disabled in each of these regions.

The DISPCNT Register
DISPCNT Bits 13-15 are used to enable Window 0, Window 1, and/or OBJ Window
regions, if any of these regions is enabled then the "Outside of Windows"
region is automatically enabled, too.
DISPCNT Bits 8-12 are kept used as master enable bits for the BG0-3,OBJ layers,
a layer is displayed only if both DISPCNT and WININ/OUT enable bits are set.

  LCD VRAM BG Screen Data Format (BG Map)

The display background consists of 8x8 dot tiles, the arrangement of these
tiles is specified by the BG Screen Data (BG Map). The separate entries in this
map are as follows:

Text BG Screen (2 bytes per entry)
Specifies the tile number and attributes. Note that BG tile numbers are always
specified in steps of 1 (unlike OBJ tile numbers which are using steps of two
in 256 color/1 palette mode).

  Bit   Expl.
  0-9   Tile Number     (0-1023) (a bit less in 256 color mode, because
                           there'd be otherwise no room for the bg map)
  10    Horizontal Flip (0=Normal, 1=Mirrored)
  11    Vertical Flip   (0=Normal, 1=Mirrored)
  12-15 Palette Number  (0-15)    (Not used in 256 color/1 palette mode)

A Text BG Map always consists of 32x32 entries (256x256 pixels), 400h entries =
800h bytes. However, depending on the BG Size, one, two, or four of these Maps
may be used together, allowing to create backgrounds of 256x256, 512x256,
256x512, or 512x512 pixels, if so, the first map (SC0) is located at base+0,
the next map (SC1) at base+800h, and so on.

## Report: phase3/ppu-affine-bitmap

**This branch can't be merged as-is.** It needs a small change to `src/ppu/mod.rs`, which I don't own. Without it, `cargo test` has 3 failures and the aw-arm-alu, aw-thumb-alu and memory smoke tests drop to near zero. With it, all 103 tests pass and every smoke test matches main exactly. The patch is ready at `/tmp/claude-1000/-var-www-html-test-projects-gba-trial-gba-emu/ec739230-fb4b-467b-9709-e53c38e370f4/scratchpad/mod-contract.patch`.

### 1. What I built and the commits
- `fe3a38f feat(ppu): affine backgrounds with wraparound and 128-1024 sizes`
  - `/var/www/html/test-projects/gba-trial/gba-emu/.claude/worktrees/agent-ad24e8a2be3196f5d/src/ppu/bg_affine.rs`
  - 8bpp tiles, one-byte map entries, map sizes 128 to 1024, the wraparound bit, and transparent pixels outside the map when it doesn't wrap.
  - `AffineWalk` starts each line at `affine_reference_point` and steps by PA/PC with one add per pixel (no division, no allocation).
  - 3 unit tests.
- `c5362b8 feat(ppu): bitmap modes through the BG2 affine transform`
  - `/var/www/html/test-projects/gba-trial/gba-emu/.claude/worktrees/agent-ad24e8a2be3196f5d/src/ppu/bitmap.rs`
  - Modes 3, 4 and 5 now go through the BG2 transform using the same `AffineWalk`.
  - Frame select applies to modes 4 and 5 only; mode 5 is 160x128.
  - Anything outside the bitmap is transparent, and the wrap bit is ignored there, as gbatek says.
  - 2 unit tests.

### 2. Scores (`replay_score_deduped`)
All three grading runs were stopped by the system for low memory. I didn't restart them. The smoke tests finished before that; most long replays didn't.

| test | before (main 4e3eddf) | branch as committed | branch + mod.rs patch |
|---|---|---|---|
| aw-arm-alu | 0.8311 | **0.1043** | 0.8311 |
| aw-thumb-alu | 0.8328 | **0.1442** | 0.8328 |
| memory | 1.0 | **0.0** | 1.0 |
| timer-reload | 0.5396 | 0.5396 | 0.5396 |
| dma-priority | 0.9784 | 0.9784 | 0.9784 |
| tonc-snd1 | 0.9167 | 0.9167 | 0.9167 |
| piugba-gameplay | 0.3233 | 0.3233 | 0.3233 |
| bulletgba-gameplay | 0.6684 | not finished | not finished |
| spout, celeste, varooom-3d | not finished | not finished | not finished |

Dev ROMs, run locally with the mod.rs patch:
- **sbb-aff and m7-demo:** render correctly.
- **ppu-bgx:** a solid green screen, which most likely means pass.
- **bm-modes and pageflip:** show a picture with the patch. Without it they collapse to a single colour.
- **ppu-bgpd:** shows a gradient, but I couldn't tell whether it's correct.

`cargo build --release --lib --target wasm32-unknown-unknown` succeeds.

### 3. Contract change needed, and guesses
**Change needed in `src/ppu/mod.rs`:**
- In `Ppu::new`, set BG2PA, BG2PD, BG3PA and BG3PD to 0x100 (1.0).
- Many ROMs, including the tonc demos and the aw and memory test ROMs, never write these registers but still expect an unscaled bitmap. At 0 every pixel samples the same texel.
- gbatek doesn't give a reset value, and the BIOS stub doesn't write these registers. So 1.0 at power-on is a guess, backed by how those ROMs are written and how they render in Mesen2's reference frames.

**Three mod.rs tests need updating** because they call `render_line(n)` without the reference point having moved to line n:
- `mode3_…` and `mode5_…` now set BG2Y to `line << 8` first.
- `affine_reference_point_reloads_…` now expects `(-128, 256)`, because PD is 1.0 at power-on.

The patch covers all of these.

**Not finished:**
- The long-replay scores (above).
- BG mosaic for affine and bitmap layers. Both files have a `ponytail:` note for it.

### 4. NOTES.md entries
- 2026-11-05: BG2/BG3 PA and PD power on as 0x100. gbatek gives no reset value, but bitmap-mode ROMs rely on it.
- 2026-11-05: Bitmap modes reuse the affine walker (`bg_affine::AffineWalk`). Pixels outside the bitmap are always transparent and the wrap bit is ignored, per gbatek "Area Overflow".
- 2026-11-05: Affine and bitmap layers skip BG mosaic for now; the effects worker owns mosaic.

**Next step:** apply the patch, then rerun the long replays when there's enough memory (`scripts/grade-subset.sh … spout-gameplay celeste-gameplay varooom-3d-gameplay bulletgba-gameplay`, one at a time).

You are a lazy senior developer. Lazy means efficient, not careless. You have
seen every over-engineered codebase and been paged at 3am for one. The best

ACTIVE EVERY RESPONSE. No drift back to over-building. Still active if
unsure. Off only: "stop ponytail" / "normal mode". Default: **full**.
Switch: `/ponytail lite|full|ultra`.

## The ladder

Stop at the first rung that holds:

1. **Does this need to exist at all?** Speculative need = skip it, say so in one line. (YAGNI)
2. **Already in this codebase?** A helper, util, type, or pattern that already lives here → reuse it. Look before you write; re-implementing what's a few files over is the most common slop.
3. **Stdlib does it?** Use it.
4. **Native platform feature covers it?** `<input type="date">` over a picker lib, CSS over JS, DB constraint over app code.
5. **Already-installed dependency solves it?** Use it. Never add a new one for what a few lines can do.
6. **Can it be one line?** One line.
7. **Only then:** the minimum code that works.

The ladder is a reflex, not a research project — but it runs *after* you
understand the problem, not instead of it. Read the task and the code it
touches first, trace the real flow end to end, then climb. Two rungs work →
take the higher one and move on. The first lazy solution that works is the
right one — once you actually know what the change has to touch.

**Bug fix = root cause, not symptom.** A report names a symptom. Before you
edit, grep every caller of the function you're about to touch. The lazy fix IS
the root-cause fix: one guard in the shared function is a smaller diff than a
guard in every caller — and patching only the path the ticket names leaves
every sibling caller still broken. Fix it once, where all callers route through.

## Rules

- No unrequested abstractions: no interface with one implementation, no factory for one product, no config for a value that never changes.
- No boilerplate, no scaffolding "for later", later can scaffold for itself.
- Deletion over addition. Boring over clever, clever is what someone decodes at 3am.

- Complex request? Ship the lazy version and question it in the same response, "Did X; Y covers it. Need full X? Say so." Never stall on an answer you can default.
- Two stdlib options, same size? Take the one that's correct on edge cases. Lazy means writing less code, not picking the flimsier algorithm.
- Mark deliberate simplifications that cut a real corner with a known ceiling (global lock, O(n²) scan, naive heuristic) with a `ponytail:` comment naming the ceiling and upgrade path (`# ponytail: global lock, per-account locks if throughput matters`).

## Output

Code first. Then at most three short lines: what was skipped, when to add it.
No essays, no feature tours, no design notes. If the explanation is longer
than the code, delete the explanation, every paragraph defending a
simplification is complexity smuggled back in as prose. Explanation the user
explicitly asked for (a report, a walkthrough, per-phase notes) is not debt,
give it in full, the rule is only against unrequested prose.

| Level | What change |
|-------|------------|

### 3. Contract change needed, and guesses
**Change needed in `src/ppu/mod.rs`:**
- In `Ppu::new`, set BG2PA, BG2PD, BG3PA and BG3PD to 0x100 (1.0).
- Many ROMs, including the tonc demos and the aw and memory test ROMs, never write these registers but still expect an unscaled bitmap. At 0 every pixel samples the same texel.
- gbatek doesn't give a reset value, and the BIOS stub doesn't write these registers. So 1.0 at power-on is a guess, backed by how those ROMs are written and how they render in Mesen2's reference frames.

**Three mod.rs tests need updating** because they call `render_line(n)` without the reference point having moved to line n:
- `mode3_…` and `mode5_…` now set BG2Y to `line << 8` first.
- `affine_reference_point_reloads_…` now expects `(-128, 256)`, because PD is 1.0 at power-on.

The patch covers all of these.
